summary: Route-level tariff misapplied during canary rollout causing unexpected invoice spike
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NimbleAI reports a sudden ~42% increase in their latest invoice (billing period ending 2026-03-11). The spike correlates with requests from a single production route that was included in a canary rollout on 2026-03-11.

Impact:
- Customer sees a $12,400 unexpected line on invoice for the week of 2026-03-04 to 2026-03-11.
- Affected routes show higher per-token unit cost for ~6 hours during the canary window.
- Customer is enterprise and flagged for escalation; they are threatening to pause production traffic if unresolved.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east-1, hosted API behind api-gateway.
- Canary rollout: traffic-split policy 'route-tier-canary-2026-03' applied at 10:00 UTC on 2026-03-11.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Canary toggled at 10:00 UTC on 2026-03-11 (rolling 5% -> 25% -> 50%).
2) Around 10:06 UTC billing meter logs started receiving requests tagged with route_id 'nimble-conv-v1' and an unexpected tag 'tariff:reserved-2025' in addition to normal customer_rate tags.
3) Serving runtime routed some requests to a dedicated pool for latency SLOs (intended), but metering picked up the canary tag precedence incorrectly and applied a different tariff mapping.
4) Metering aggregator emitted postbacks between 10:06-16:30 UTC with rate_id that maps to an expensive reserved-rate plan; downstream billing included those at reserved_rate instead of hosted_rate or reserved-override.

Logs / evidence:
- Billing dashboard (Billing > Postbacks > 2026-03-11) shows spike for org nimbleai-org-88 between 10:05-16:40 UTC.
- Datadog trace ids: trace: dd-acc-7742, dd-acc-7748 correlating to canary rollout API calls.
- Metering service postback samples attached in investigation notes and linked PR.
- Slack thread: #support (link in comments).

Customer request:
- Immediate provisional credit to cover the overbilled amount while we investigate.
- Clear explanation of root cause and confirmation that this will not recur.
comments: 2026-03-12 08:22 - Aisha Patel: Logged at customer request. Customer provided invoice PDF and relevant route_id. Asked for escalation as enterprise tier.
2026-03-12 09:10 - Noah Kim: Assigned. Elevated to billing + routing eng. Kicked off triage; asked for earliest telemetry export for route nimble-conv-v1.

2026-03-12 11:02 - Billing Team (via INT-1204): We see ~18k postbacks tagged with tariff:reserved-2025 for nimbleai-org-88 during canary period. Exporting samples to S3 (s3://billing-exports/sup-988001/).

2026-03-12 14:35 - Routing Eng (Elena Rossi): Preliminary hypothesis: canary tag decorator service applied 'tariff' tag at route-level and the metering precedence logic treats route-level tariff with higher priority than customer rate_id. That precedence was changed in rollout PR #4321.

2026-03-13 09:44 - Customer (Kyle Martinez, NimbleAI): Appreciates quick response. Asked for a provisional credit and confirmation we have reverted canary. Also asked whether this affects historical invoices.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Noah Kim: Canary rolled back at 2026-03-12 17:00 UTC. Billing team applied provisional invoice hold and started a credit calculation. Informing customer of rollback and next steps.

2026-03-14 10:30 - Billing Lead (Priya Shah): Provisional credit calculated (see investigation notes). Issued credit memo CM-2026-03-SUP988001 for $12,400 against nimbleai-org-88 pending final reconciliation.
investigation_notes: Datadog query (postbacks.per_minute{org:nimbleai-org-88,region:us-east-1}): spike 10:05-16:40 UTC, avg unit_price jumped from $0.0008 -> $0.0019

Related PR that touched tag precedence: https://github.com/redwood-infra/meters/pull/4321 (merged 2026-03-10) — introduced 'route_tariff' tag which unintentionally supersedes explicit 'customer_rate_id' when both present
Query of metering aggregator code confirmed a bug: precedence if (hasTag('route_tariff')) then use route rate else fallback — needs fallback check for 'customer_owned_rate'
Audit: only 6 enterprise orgs temporarily had this tag during the canary window (subset included NimbleAI). No evidence of historical re-tagging outside the window.
resolution:
Temporary measures: canary disabled 2026-03-12 17:00 UTC. Billing placed provisional hold and issued CM-2026-03-SUP988001 for $12,400 to NimbleAI. Engineering hotfix merged to meters service to respect explicit customer_rate_id over route_tariff when customer_rate is present (PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/meters/pull/4337).

Follow-ups: schedule a canary re-run with additional telemetry check (owner: routing eng), run reconciliation job for 2026-03 invoice cycle to ensure no residual misbilled postbacks (owner: billing), add synthetic test in CI to assert tariff precedence, and add alerting on postback unit_price deltas > 50% within 6h for enterprise customers.

Customer communication: Sent interim explanation and credit memo; will follow up with root cause report and postmortem after reconciliation.
